title: Secure build, test, and release supply chains: decision comparison 1
teachingQuestion: What chain of evidence shows that a deployed artifact was built from approved source and dependencies in a protected process?
focalInsight: CI/CD stages, configuration baseline, build integrity, artifact/software provenance, dependency management, and complementary SAST/DAST/SCA/IAST evidence.
caption: Compare meaning, decision conditions, and failures. These concise distinctions are paired with the worked examples in the teaching unit.

nodes.label: Ci Cd
nodes.definition: Automated and governed continuous integration/continuous delivery pipeline practices that build, test, package, and promote change through environments.
nodes.decision: Separate pipeline roles/environments and define required evidence and authorization before promotion.
nodes.failureExample: A pipeline credential able to alter source, build, and production creates an unchecked path to deployment.
nodes.detail: Automated and governed continuous integration/continuous delivery pipeline practices that build, test, package, and promote change through environments.

nodes.label: Continuous Integration
nodes.definition: Frequent integration of changes into a shared codebase with automated build and test feedback.
nodes.decision: Use to discover integration defects quickly while protecting the source revision and test environment.
nodes.failureExample: Passing a unit build does not prove the merged application or release artifact is authorized.
nodes.detail: Frequent integration of changes into a shared codebase with automated build and test feedback.

nodes.label: Continuous Delivery
nodes.definition: Capability to keep validated changes ready for controlled production release, with promotion evidence and release decisions.
nodes.decision: Require explicit policy/approval and environment safeguards even when deployment can be automated.
nodes.failureExample: Automatically releasing every ready artifact can expose customers to an unreviewed high-impact change.
nodes.detail: Capability to keep validated changes ready for controlled production release, with promotion evidence and release decisions.

nodes.label: Configuration Management
nodes.definition: Control of identified configuration items, versions, authorized changes, baselines, status, and reproducibility.
nodes.decision: Name artifacts and allowable states, control entry/change, and preserve the baseline needed for rollback and investigation.
nodes.failureExample: An unknown production configuration makes it impossible to reproduce, verify, or safely reverse a release.
nodes.detail: Control of identified configuration items, versions, authorized changes, baselines, status, and reproducibility.

nodes.label: Build Integrity
nodes.definition: Assurance that the build process, runner, inputs, configuration, and outputs were protected from unauthorized alteration.
nodes.decision: Use isolated/maintained runners, constrained identities, protected configuration, logs, and response procedures for suspected compromise.
nodes.failureExample: A compromised build runner can inject code after source review and before artifact signing.
nodes.detail: Assurance that the build process, runner, inputs, configuration, and outputs were protected from unauthorized alteration.

nodes.label: Artifact Provenance
nodes.definition: Evidence linking a released artifact to its source revision, dependencies, build process, identity, tests, and authorized promotion.
nodes.decision: Verify digest/attestation/signing and promotion records before deployment; preserve enough evidence to investigate or reproduce.
nodes.failureExample: An artifact name and version label alone cannot prove what source or builder produced it.
nodes.detail: Evidence linking a released artifact to its source revision, dependencies, build process, identity, tests, and authorized promotion.

nodes.label: Sast
nodes.definition: Static application security testing analyzes source, bytecode, or representations without executing the application.
nodes.decision: Use early to find code-pattern issues and triage findings with context; it cannot prove runtime configuration or all exploitability.
nodes.failureExample: Treating SAST silence as proof of secure authentication misses deployment and business-logic failures.
nodes.detail: Static application security testing analyzes source, bytecode, or representations without executing the application.

nodes.label: Dast
nodes.definition: Dynamic application security testing exercises a running application from outside to observe security behavior.
nodes.decision: Use against a controlled, representative running target and interpret coverage/authorization limits.
nodes.failureExample: A DAST scan that lacks an authenticated role cannot establish that privileged authorization is sound.
nodes.detail: Dynamic application security testing exercises a running application from outside to observe security behavior.

nodes.label: Sca
nodes.definition: Software composition analysis identifies included third-party components and associated known-risk/license information.
nodes.decision: Use with dependency inventory, provenance, version policy, and remediation ownership; distinguish known-CVE status from integrity and fitness.
nodes.failureExample: A clean SCA result does not prove the dependency came from an approved source or has no unknown flaw.
nodes.detail: Software composition analysis identifies included third-party components and associated known-risk/license information.

learningContract.teachingQuestion: What chain of evidence shows that a deployed artifact was built from approved source and dependencies in a protected process?
learningContract.misconception: An SBOM, clean scanner result, or successful build alone proves the released artifact is trustworthy.
learningContract.formRationale: Aligned columns make concept meanings, decision criteria and failure consequences explicit and comparable.
learningContract.focalInsight: CI/CD stages, configuration baseline, build integrity, artifact/software provenance, dependency management, and complementary SAST/DAST/SCA/IAST evidence.
learningContract.intentionalOmissions: Do not require a particular CI/CD vendor, signing scheme, artifact format, or universal policy threshold.
learningContract.retrievalPrompt: SCA is clean but the artifact came from an unreviewed branch and shared runner. Which provenance claims remain unproved?
